Iran's Industrialization: So Far, So Hard

The Story of Failure in Industrialization

In the early 2000s, Masoud Nili drafted Iran's industrial development strategy, but he believes the governance of that era lacked the capacity to approve and implement it. Two decades later, he and his colleagues reexamined Iran's industrial trends and laid out the challenges facing Iran's industrialization.

Watch the conversation: https://youtu.be/sIpPKMNfrRY

In this conversation, Masoud Nili shows in detail what industrialization is, what its social effects are, what consequences de-industrialization has had for Iranian society, and what mechanisms in domestic politics and sanctions caused Iran's industry to decline from the mid-2000s onward. Ultimately, by comparing Iran's situation with four different categories of countries, he analyzes the effects of economic governance on industrialization.

A significant part of this conversation addresses the developments that have taken place on the global stage and in geopolitical and geoeconomic disputes, and the efforts of countries around the world to position themselves within the global economic system and benefit from it.

The Young Generation: From Protester to Hezbollahi

This program was recorded on Shahrivar 5, 1405.

Can it be said that Gen Z has only one political orientation? Or does the young generation and Gen Z possess their own particular multiplicity and complexity? In this episode, Mostafa Nozari, criticizing Navid_Kolharoudi, moves beyond the one-dimensional representation of the young generation as protesters and shows another facet of this generation. Watch the conversation https://youtu.be/SlojnJh7YZo

Mostafa Nozari, who has a pluralistic and complex lived experience, believes that ignoring the Hezbollahi youth can be bloody; and he speaks of the necessity of a different social perspective on Iranian society.
